contradictions.topic: Which UI generation the Workflows click paths describe - the corpus states both, in the same version

readings.summary: The Workflows guide's own revision history, dated September 2025, says the Workflows tool documentation was updated to the NEW UI - implying the screens and paths shown are current-generation and that no legacy twin survives.
readings.sourceQuote: Updated images and text to the new UI for the Workflows Tool and Edit and Delete Worflows, Properties, and Steps sections.

readings.summary: A tools-guides topic in the same corpus version describes the administrator reaching Authorized Approvers from workflows in the CLASSIC interface.
readings.sourceQuote: the Invoice Configuration administrator uses the Authorized Approvers link from workflows in the classic interface

contradictions.consequenceForWriter: Set uiVariant 'undifferentiated' on every Workflows record and treat every navPath as UNVERIFIED as to UI generation. An automation must probe for the element and fail soft rather than assert a path; if the first click path misses, the correct hypothesis is a UI-generation mismatch, not a wrong label. Do not claim 'both' - nobody has read two variants of this page.
contradictions.notes: Hypothesis: SAP revised the Workflows admin topics in place for the new UI but left older cross-references in the tools guides un-updated. Supporting observation, not proof: the corpus DOES draw the distinction explicitly elsewhere - approval-flow-page-c73e063f.md contrasts the legacy UI and the new UI for the end-user Approval Flow page - so the absence of any such sentence for the admin Workflows surface is a documentation gap, not evidence of a single UI. There is no *-new-experience-* twin for any workflow file. TEXT TRAP: the revision line misspells 'Worflows' (once corpus-wide).

contradictions.topic: The Settings surface inside Workflows is named four different ways

readings.sourceQuote: Settings tab and is shown in the following figure.

readings.summary: Calls it the Settings section of the Workflows tool.
readings.sourceQuote: you must clear a setting in the Settings section of the Workflows tool

readings.summary: Calls it the Settings page, in a cross-reference from the General-page roster.
readings.sourceQuote: field on the Settings page cleared (disabled)

contradictions.consequenceForWriter: Treat all four as one surface. A driver should locate the tab by the visible string 'Settings' inside the Workflows page and must NOT search for a separate page named 'Workflow Settings'. Never name these controls 'Invoice Settings' - that title belongs to a different, already-built page and merging them would corrupt both.

contradictions.topic: Two Settings-tab controls are named with 'invoice' in one file and 'payment request' in another

readings.summary: The settings table names the control with 'payment request'.
readings.sourceQuote: Filter payment request items to those that are applicable to Cost Object

readings.summary: The guide's revision history announces the same new Settings-tab option with 'invoice'.
readings.sourceQuote: Filter invoice items to those that are applicable to Cost Object

contradictions.consequenceForWriter: Record both label forms as aliases of one control and have the driver probe 'Filter payment request items...' first, falling back to 'Filter invoice items...'. The same drift applies to the recall control: 'Allow processor to recall a payment request to last processor step' (invoice-settings-cace748d.md) versus 'Allow processor to recall an invoice to last processor step' (general-information-8b3b0308.md). Matching on one form alone WILL fail on a tenant rendering the other.
contradictions.notes: Hypothesis: the release-note text was written against the older 'invoice' vocabulary and the settings table was later re-worded to the 'payment request' object name; SAP uses both terms for the same object throughout this corpus. Which string the UI actually renders is not determinable from documentation.

contradictions.topic: The four General-page workflow timeout controls are named differently in the Vendor Approval topic

readings.summary: The primary General-page roster names the timeout controls Approval Time Expired Action and Assignment Timeout Action.
readings.sourceQuote: This option is only available if either the Approval Time Expired Action or Assignment Timeout Action options are enabled.

readings.summary: The Vendor Approval topic names the same behaviour Workflow Step Timeout Duration and Approval Action.
readings.sourceQuote: The Workflow Step Timeout Duration setting specifies the number of days an invoice can remain at a workflow step before it times out.

contradictions.consequenceForWriter: Do NOT create separate fields for Workflow Step Timeout Duration or Approval Action - treat them as alternative descriptive names for the documented General-page timeout family (Approval Time Expired Action, Expire After This Many Days, Assignment Timeout Action, Allow Timeout Extensions for This Many Days). A driver should look for the 554e86aa labels and only fall back to the b3d1bd2c wording.
contradictions.notes: Hypothesis: b3d1bd2c is a Vendor-guide topic describing the timeout behaviour generically rather than quoting the UI. It is a LABEL contradiction, not evidence of extra fields; the recon's earlier reading of these as homeless orphan fields was wrong. appliesTo is attached to a General-page field because the contradiction is about General-page controls; no timeout field is emitted by this lens.

contradictions.topic: Which role may use the Workflows surface

readings.summary: The Workflows tool identity topic grants view and use to the Global and Group Invoice Configuration administrators and never mentions a Restricted role.
readings.sourceQuote: Both the Global Invoice Configuration administrator and the Group Invoice Configuration administrator can view the Workflows tool.

readings.summary: The Reason Category and Codes topic REQUIRES the Restricted role to use that tab's options, and then walks a write flow (New, Save).
readings.sourceQuote: The Invoice Configuration administrator (_Restricted_) role is required to use the options on this tab.

contradictions.consequenceForWriter: Do not assume one role opens the whole page. Provision an unrestricted Global Invoice Configuration administrator for the workflow object, steps and Settings tab, and separately confirm write access on the Reason Category and Codes tab before automating New/Save there. A permission wall on Workflows is most likely to appear on that tab.
contradictions.notes: Hypothesis: the Restricted role was scoped to reason codes only and the two guides were never reconciled. A July 2025 release note is reported to make that same Restricted role READ-ONLY on Workflows with New/Copy/Remove disabled, which would be a THIRD reading - release notes are not a citable sourceFile in this graph, so it is recorded here as unverified context, not as a reading. overview-9c8ca06e.md agrees with b2b61596 that the Restricted role creates the codes.

contradictions.topic: Workflows page named singular and plural in adjacent sentences of one file

readings.sourceQuote: On the Workflow page, admin will see the Require Hardcopy Receipts option.

readings.summary: Plural, in the very next sentence of the same file: 'the Workflows page'.
readings.sourceQuote: the Require Hardcopy Receipts option on the Workflows page

contradictions.consequenceForWriter: Match the page and its tabs on a case-insensitive prefix ('Workflow') rather than an exact string. The same singular/plural drift is measured across the corpus for the tab, tool, Email Notification(s), Confirmation Agreement(s) and Authorized Approver(s) labels; never gate an automation on the trailing 's'.

readings.summary: The Exceptions page, already built in this graph, documents the exception level itself as starting at ZERO, and explicitly gives 0 a meaning (non-urgent).

contradictions.consequenceForWriter: DO NOT RECONCILE. Write exception levels in the range 1-99 when setting the three Workflows Settings-tab thresholds, and permit 0 only where the Exceptions page itself is being configured. If a driver needs a value that disables the threshold, the corpus does not document one - leave the field alone rather than writing 0 to a Workflows threshold.
contradictions.notes: Hypothesis, not a finding: the two fields are different things - the Exceptions page assigns a level to an exception (where 0 is a legitimate 'non-urgent' level), while the Settings-tab controls set a THRESHOLD above which submission or transmission is blocked, for which a threshold of 0 would be meaningless. That would make both statements correct and the apparent conflict an artefact of comparing two different fields. The corpus never says so, so the discrepancy is recorded rather than explained away.

notes:
LENS C (tools-guides and cross-cutting). TOOLS-GUIDES WAS EXHAUSTED FIRST AND YIELDED ZERO FIELDS - that is the finding, not a shortfall. The three prescribed sweeps were run over all 650 tools-guides files: 'Invoice Configuration administrator' returns 16 files, '(left menu)' returns 10, 'Invoice Processing Admin' returns 4, and none of the intersecting topics configures a Workflows control. Every workflow-bearing tools-guides topic is RUNTIME (processor/approver behaviour): add-approval-steps-2e17fab0, send-an-invoice-to-an-additional-approver-afd572de, view-the-approval-workflow-of-an-invoice-d8046bec, purchase-request-approver-experience-8b50b701. Tools-guides did earn its keep three ways, all recorded above: (a) the uiVariant COUNTER-EVIDENCE in how-single-step-approval-workflow-works-40145f24.md ('the classic interface'), which is one of the two readings of the uiVariant contradiction; (b) INDEPENDENT CORROBORATION of two admin controls - automatically-transmit-purchase-orders-f1b1147c.md for the auto-transmit option and recall-invoice-to-last-processor-step-27ae1061.md for the recall setting, the latter also independently naming the Invoice Configuration Administrator role and warning that a recall ignores any workflow skip step; (c) the end-user Profile precondition for notification delivery (6d58db17). The two the-query-builder-and-the-condition-editor-*.md files were deliberately NOT read as field sources: they are the Processor RUNTIME Query Builder. So admin-guides is the field source for this page and tools-guides is corroboration only, exactly as the brief predicted. This does NOT relieve the graph's admin-guides skew; it documents why it cannot be relieved here.

uiVariant IS 'undifferentiated' ON EVERY RECORD AND THAT IS THE HONEST ANSWER, NOT A DEFAULT. A corpus-wide search for 'new experience', 'new ui', 'legacy' and 'current user interface' across BOTH guide directories returns no workflow-domain file except approval-flow-page-c73e063f.md - and that topic is the END-USER Approval Flow page, where the corpus DOES draw the distinction explicitly ('in the legacy UI. In the new UI, users click Actions > Approval Flow.'). The corpus is therefore capable of marking UI generation and simply does not do it for the admin Workflows surface, while two dated statements point in opposite directions. NO 'both' CLAIM IS MADE ANYWHERE IN THIS FILE - nobody read two variants of any Workflows screen. THE CONSEQUENCE IS LARGER THAN ANY FIELD: click paths are the only knowledge a driver cannot re-derive at runtime, so if they describe a superseded UI, every navPath fails at once.

WHAT I COULD NOT DETERMINE. (1) Whether 'Restrict approvers to those with limit authority' (definition-of-amount-for-limit-approval-06806875.md) is the same control as the longer General-page label 'Restrict approvers to those with limit authority for employee-added steps' in create-a-new-workflow-554e86aa.md, or a second step-level control. Emitted once, under the short label, with the ambiguity stated - not silently merged and not duplicated. (2) The Reason Category value list: no category is enumerated anywhere in this corpus, so validValues is empty. THIN IS THE CORRECT ANSWER. (3) Any numeric range for Minimum/Maximum Exception Level on the Authorized Approvers > Configuration sub-tab - the 'one to 99' range belongs to the Settings-tab threshold controls and was deliberately NOT borrowed. (4) Whether the Find workflow emails where list offers more than two families on a differently-provisioned site. (5) Which of the two label forms each drifted control actually renders.

NO VALUE WAS COMPLETED. steps_can_be_added_by carries two values because ONE cross-cutting topic enumerates two; the primary roster enumerates none, and workflow-creation-process-1d37b85f.md writes 'Approver' where approve-forward-feature-b847d65b.md writes 'Approver Only' - both strings are recorded in the value set's notes rather than reconciled. consolidate_pr_items_same_vendor carries two values because the source states BOTH, which is the legitimate opposite of the invented Yes values previously deleted from this graph.
